reviews.text: This game is so good. I love that there's a story and a Roguelike game mode. It's a lot of fun to explore and shoot and customize your Loadout.

It's good so far. I appreciate the polish on quality of life right on release, nothing feels janky, it's very smooth. I haven't encountered any bugs or issues after several missions. I particularly like the option for auto-aim. Being able to customize the main character's appearance would be nice, but maybe that's something that can be unlocked later. Review left at 1.1 hours of playtime.
Lot of fun. Quick pace and easy to pick up and play.

I'm really enjoying this game. It has a nice balance of action, exploring, and crafting. I recommend paying attention to your load outs, I didn't do that at first. But you end up with a cache of items and mixing up your load outs can help with different maps. I also recommend taking the time to explore all areas of each map, there's good loot to find that you'll want later in the game. There's a lot of enemy variety, and things can get intense fast. I don't want to spoil anything, but there will be times where you're dodging and shooting from all angles with no relief in sight. The soundtrack is awesome too. And if you have someone to play with, the co-op mode is really fun.

When I played the nextfest demo for Vortica, I fell in love with it immediately and put it on my "buy on release" list. Now that the release is here, I'm happy to say that Vortica has only gotten better. A wide variety of weapons and tools, rad music, well thought out mechanics, wild enemies, a good grimdark story and an impressive attention to little details. It's an interesting mix of top down shooter and tower defense, and we can change our loadout to focus heavily on one if we want. Some of my complaints made during the nextfest are still here though. There is no gallery of monsters we can look at (I want more lore!), enemy weaknesses are still mostly discovered through trial and error and map modifiers are not explained (again an emphasis on trial and error). These are minor qualms though, and it can be fun to go into a map blind and then see everyone's shots spiraling all over the place because of a spatial or magnetic anomaly. I might have planned my loadout differently if I knew what those did in advance, but learning through trial and error feels nostalgic.
This is such a fun game that I just can’t stop thinking about! I’m excited to see where the devs take things. Give it a try!

Thought this game looked cool and it didn't disappoint. Gameplay and controls feel pretty smooth, lighting is amazing and pixel art is nice looking too. I like the variety of stages and lots of different enemies so far. Also 10/10 Synthwave soundtrack! My only gripes so far are same-ish mission objectives and also they feel a bit short overall. Definitely feels like it could be an indie classic!

Very fun game especially with coop. Good level of intensity, and a few enemies that might terrify you on a first encounter. Very very reminiscent of older Xbox 360 arcade titles, would have loved to play this back in the day, and it feels great even now.

Overall Impression: Solid A. A great game that does not waste your time or insult your intelligence. On normal, things are a bit tough. If your are looking for an more relaxed game, set it on easy. It will teach you the ropes and then will let you decide if you want to try the higher levels of difficulty. For the money, this is an easy recommend for anyone who likes this kind of game.

Many people have asked for this game to become a roguelike, as of writing this it is under false-advertising. It is not a roguelike in that you cannot replay any levels or have any way to improve your character. Once you get to the boss level, you are locked at your current power level with no other gameplay to do than to attempt to fight the boss that you are not strong enough to kill, therefore literally unplayable.

Vortica is a great little game to dive into! It has an "adventure" mode with a light story (datapads and text entries to find, and a structured progression) and a rougelite mode that I've yet to try, and a nice soundtrack. There appear to be a good variety of enemies, weapons, and gadgets. All have felt pretty good and fun to use so far. You get to tailor your loadout for each mission to deal with the enemy types and environmental hazards which are presented before you embark. My feedback for now would be to improve the map generation, you end up seeing a lot of areas that make no sense, pointless doors, and a bit maze like at times. And this next point could actually be a pro for some people, the missions are pretty short, like 5-10 minutes short. This does run very well on the steam deck so that can be a pro for very short game sessions where you can feel like you still made progress. Anyway, congrats to the dev for making a fun game and shipping it!
FOR STEAMDECK PLAYERS: in later levels, graphics go to sh*t. Too many enemies, projectiles, etc. cause the game to go to 2 fps. @Developers: please fix this. other than that, game is decent.

The game destroys itself from the constant warping. The destroy all Vortal missions are especially horrible. No screen shake options is always a huge minus as well. I tried to like this game but its poorly optimized for what it is forcing to occur while playing.
eh

This is a small but fun game that really worked to have as an in between game. There is a good variety of weapons and gadgets to to choose from and experiment with for particular missions to be more efficient. The missions are also short and sweet but have some difficult ones that will have you scrambling through hordes or a bullet hell. For the price point I think it is a great game. It will last you between 6 to 8 hours for a complete playthrough of all missions. I really hope there is more content to come for this.

This is a fun game to play while working out. Ill sit on my spin bike or treadmill for two hours will pass by with barely any notice. It's frustrating at times, but good games like this one make you adapt to changing conditions and offer several ways to overcome the challenges.

The beginning of the game seems fine at first and neat game easy to understand etc. love the graphics and game play. When doing loadouts, the big weapons suck because they require too much space in the loadout and too time to either recharge or reload even with the added passives when your in a bind that requires quick action against a bunch of aliens, but later when you get towards the end, the monoliths just rip you a new one and can't get past the overwhelming amounts of them that keeps spawning, Monoliths need to be toned down a bit and spawn rate of them shouldn't be crazy amounts. maybe its just me but monoliths even on normal difficulty solo is just impossible to get past when they spawn and spawn and no way to get to the vortal with out like 10 of them killing you all at the same time. I'm on the second to last mission, the galaxy garden mission and just can't do it solo, impossible, tried for about 4 hours straight with various loadouts and no matter what I'm overwhelmed and over powered by monoliths, I can clear the beginning but its getting back out to the portal is the problem, by the time i get the vorizum and attempt to fight back I'm met with impossible odds. I might just skip this mission. After playing around with some loadouts and attempting the last mission i couldn't beat, I was able to finally brain storm how to pass it even though it was a horrible vortal spot to get back to, great game for the price, I would say so.

I wish Steam had a neutral option. The first few planets felt too easy and then the game jumps to a difficulty that is almost unplayable. Could be a skill issue on my end, maybe. I love the graphics and the soundtrack. I love the overall gameplay, albeit it starts to feel repetitive. I'm one planet away from Earth and after dying several times on my last level, I finally just did the objective and ran, taking damage along the way. After that, I just don't have the drive to keep playing until the end. It's clear the game gives you challenges so you can change up your loadout, which I am all here for, but it doesn't give you nearly enough slots to have an effective loadout. Any buffs to bullet damage or reload speed also seem totally unnoticeable. It's obvious the devs are passionate about their game and did such a fantastic job with it. I can't give this a negative review but I would like to see more balance in the gameplay before I return to it.
I really enjoy this game after work, the atmosphere and BGM is very well done. I hope this game succeeds.
Yeah it's good. I feel like it's pretty unique in its gameplay style. Not really much else to say, but you'll have a fun time!

I enjoyed the first couple hours for sure. After the first boss I was finding that not only was it starting to be boring with repetitive missions, the enemies were getting far more health than what my weapons could output. Eventually I had to lean on turrets to clear what used to be simple rooms. Towards the later levels in particular, if there were more than 4 enemies, my AA-12 shotgun simply wasn't enough. I tried switching to several different weapons like the mp5, P-Shooter (the only particle weapon I ever found), and several of the heat weapons but these enemies would easily soak up the damage I could deal and swarm me very quickly. I recommend people stay away from this one. If you really want to see what the good part is like, play the demo. after that, it's basically all down hill.

The game has serious and widespread game-breaking issues that prevent progress and completion in many different ways. From spending 10 hours to get a save that crashes to desktop every time it's opened, to spending 8 hours on a new save that is softlocked because of map generation failure, this game is not in a suitable state for a commercial release. If at some point this game has undergone a massive overhaul of rigorous testing and fixing, I might go back and try my currently-worthless saves again to see if the game can be finished. I would not start a new game just for that, and I do NOT recommend this game to anyone. As it stands, it's a waste of time.

游戏点子不错，后期变身人型高达的点子很好，你可以同时操作不少武器，只要键位还有空。但是游戏难度平衡问题很大，首先是一直缺钱，因为你的负重和血量都大部分需要钱来做，系统还不允许你在低难度刷钱，做完就消失了，主线任务里几乎是推着你往越高难走，然后稀里糊涂打过第一场boss战后就是难度逆天的转折点了，后期的敌人会像疯了一样刷出来，长得像墓碑的monolith血又厚蓄力激光又快又准，1个已经很不好躲了，关闭刷兵传送门的任务它还库库刷，你干掉它的速度根本比不上它出来的速度，低重力环境下它能把你抽的像陀螺一样旋转。严重怀疑官方有没有设计过后期任务的难度曲线。

Game is too annoying to be fun, loadout system is straight garbage, boss fights are tedious, some of the levels just make me want to tear my hair out. Combined with no bestiary and all the enemies feeling the same leads to frustration with choosing the correct loadout each time because some weapons will do basically no damage to the enemies. The levels all feel the same, basically the gunplay/combat is supposed to be the highlight of this game and it just falls so flat. The turrets especially are touted as being the big thing, but they're all so tedious to operate and so annoying. At this point I'm forcing myself to play because I'm over the 2 hour mark, the game was sorta fun for the first bit but now it's pure tedium and one annoyance after the other. Not to mention the story is so uninspired and uninteresting, it's like the game had so much potential but squanders it all

This game was fine and it worked fine, but I just didn't find it that fun. I think it needed some better enemy design, or better writing or something. Also found the bosses pretty uninspired. It absolutely works and is well made and does what it says on the tin. So if it looks really interesting to you I would get it. But it didn't quite hit with me and I have a million games, so I cannot recommend it.
6/10 Gets stale quite quickly and I feel no inclination to play through it again. But, it's solid enough and quite fun whilst it lasts but nothing ground breaking. Wait for a sale to be blunt.

I liked it. It has good and bad sides. I think it is enough of a starting point to further expand in a sequel. Not a single issue during my playthrough. Played it shamelessly on easier difficulty because I don't like sweating too much with video games. Enemies were fun to play against. Best map is the first map, which is tragic. Most maps feel pathetically small and uninspired, with extremely minimalistic details, that don't give any tangible identity for the place you are supposed to be in. Weapons have decent variety and are generally fun to use. Overreliance on the turrets as a mob clearer kinda constrains the gameplay but if you like playing the turret guy in games, you will like it. Loadout system also feels a bit constraining but still adds a spice to the gameplay that makes you want to plan properly for the missions. Not having a way to track the collected lore texts in the base is a crime. I have no idea what the lore is because I read about the lore in bases / lobbies :D Some items are invaluable, while some are absolutely useless and I don't even bother trying them, which is a waste of time for the dev. All items that you stumble on must have at least some minimal value for you as a player or it is just a disappointment and demerit for the game. Some items that seem useful are actually useful once or twice in the whole playthrough and you realize too late because it is not properly explained that the game mission screen specifies when they are useful and you don't use them anywhere else, and then you suffer regret for wasting loadout points on them for no reason. The base feels empty and barely utilized. Bosses are weirdly balanced and feel out of order. Last one is hilariously the easiest and the spider one is the most ridiculously brutal for some reason :D Fun but forgettable in its bland absence of eyecandy in simple moments of cool things happening or cool people doing stuff in cool places. Autor should focus on art style and lovability of the characters, diversifying the gameplay styles and adding more linear handcrafted moments in between generic combat rumble, trough better map design and maybe metroidvania progression.
折磨大于乐趣，不打算吊死在这一棵树上。
